chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the virgin whom the man marries by Mut'a. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem as long as he does not destroy her virginity.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry a virgin in Mut'a without consummating the marriage fully?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarates a specific legal nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding temporary marriage (Mut'a), asserting that the physical preservation of virginity is not a prerequisite for the validity of the contract or the permissibility of intercourse. It reflects the scholarly view that while virginity is a desirable attribute, its loss does not invalidate the marital bond, distinguishing Mut'a from permanent marriage in certain legal implications. This ruling is foundational in understanding the flexibility of Mut'a contracts within Shia fiqh.
